q: When operating the 737 Freighter, what may the flight crew wear?
a: Uniforms are not required, and casual work attire may be worn.

src.quote: When operating the 737 Freighter, uniforms are not required, and casual work attire may be worn.
src.note: This note appears under the 737 Cargo Operations section. It relaxes the normal uniform requirement specifically for 737 Freighter flying.

q: What cargo limitation applies to a Part 91 Non-Revenue positioning flight on the freighter?

src.note: The Freighter Cargo Limitations table pairs Part 91 Non-Revenue and Positioning flights with a prohibition on revenue cargo, whereas Revenue operations have no limitation on authorized revenue cargo.

q: How many persons does Alaska Airlines currently authorize as a supernumerary?
a: None. Alaska Airlines does not currently authorize any persons as a supernumerary.

src.ref: FOM 17.1.2 — Freighter Flight Deck and Supernumerary Compartment
src.quote: Currently, Alaska Airlines does not authorize any persons as a supernumerary.
src.note: Because no supernumeraries are authorized, no persons are authorized to occupy the Supernumerary Compartment on a revenue freighter flight.

src.ref: FOM 17.1.2 — Freighter Flight Deck and Supernumerary Compartment
src.quote: A supernumerary is any person on an all-cargo configured aircraft authorized by 14 CFR 121.583(a).
src.note: The definition ties supernumerary status to the regulatory allowance in 14 CFR 121.583(a) for persons carried on an all-cargo aircraft.

q: On the 800F, where is crew baggage NOT permitted to be stowed?
a: Under the 2W jumpseat or on the floor or seats of the Supernumerary Compartment.

src.quote: Baggage cannot be stowed under the 2W jumpseat or on the floor or seats of the Supernumerary Compartment
src.note: The 800F crew bag stowage rule references Flight Crew Bag Stowage guidance and prohibits these specific locations.

q: What aircraft type does Hawaiian Airlines use for Amazon Air Operations, and what is it called in the FOM?
a: The A330-343P2F, referred to in the FOM as the A330F.

src.quote: Hawaiian Airlines uses A330-343P2F aircraft for Amazon Air Operations.
src.note: To simplify documentation within the FOM, the A330-343P2F is referred to throughout as the A330F.

q: When is access to the Main Deck Cargo Compartment permitted during Amazon operations?
a: Never during flight — access is prohibited during all phases of flight.

src.ref: FOM 17.2.2.1 — Main Deck Cargo Compartment Access
src.quote: Access to the Main Deck Cargo Compartment is prohibited during all phases of flight.
src.note: This is an absolute prohibition; there is no in-flight access provision to the main deck cargo compartment.

q: What document is the official weight and balance record required by the FAA for Amazon operations?
a: The SABLE Weight and Balance Load Sheet.

src.quote: The SABLE Weight and Balance Load Sheet is the official weight and balance record required by the FAA.
src.note: It is used together with the Load Plan to confirm the aircraft is loaded within CG limits and in compliance with payload position restrictions.

q: In the normal process, by when must the Ramp PA provide the Load Sheet and Load Plan to the flight crew?
a: No later than 15 minutes prior to departure.

src.quote: the Ramp PA will provide the Load Sheet and Load Plan to the Flight Crew no later than 15 minutes prior to departure.
src.note: This applies except when using the Remote Load Verification Process. The crew carries these documents to the destination.

q: What access restriction applies to the Load Verifier during the Ramp Load Verification Process?
a: The Load Verifier must not have access to the Load Plan.

src.quote: The Load Verifier must not have access to the Load Plan.
src.note: The Load Verifier independently records ULD numbers, weights, and positions on the RLVS, then cross-checks against the Load Plan during Load Plan Validation.

q: What is the early-pushback threshold, and who must approve pushbacks earlier than that?
a: Pushbacks less than 30 minutes ahead of scheduled departure are permitted; departures more than 30 minutes ahead must be approved by the SOCC Manager on Duty (MOD) after coordination with Amazon NCC.

src.quote: pushbacks less than 30 minutes ahead of scheduled departure are permitted.
src.note: Anything more than 30 minutes ahead of scheduled pushback requires SOCC MOD approval coordinated with Amazon NCC, unless Dispatch or the Ramp PA indicates otherwise.

q: How is the Captain notified of onboard Dangerous Goods, and is eNOTOC approved for Amazon operations?
a: The Captain is notified by the NOTOC HAL 902; the eNOTOC process is not approved for Amazon operations.

src.ref: FOM 17.2.7.1 — Pilot-In-Command Notification of Onboard Dangerous Goods
src.quote: The Captain will be notified of onboard Dangerous Goods by the NOTOC HAL 902.
src.note: A hard-copy Notice-to-Captain (NOTOC HAL 902) is used; the eNOTOC process is explicitly not approved for Amazon operations.
